title: LuCa-GAIN: Gender, Acceptance and Participation in Lung Cancer Screening
summary:
Lung cancer is one of the most serious cancer diseases. If detected early, treatment can start earlier and survival chances may improve. Low-dose computed tomography can help detect lung cancer early in people at increased risk. However, screening is only effective if the relevant people are reached, understand the information, attend the appointment and return for follow-up if needed.

LuCa-GAIN examines how structured and gender-sensitive lung cancer screening can be implemented in Germany. About 2,600 people from the existing 4-IN-THE-LUNG-RUN study at DKFZ who are already eligible for lung cancer screening according to German criteria will be invited.

The project focuses on a one-stop-shop model that combines important steps: assessment of eligibility, low-dose CT, planning of possible follow-up examinations, questions on health and quality of life, personalised prevention counselling, smoking cessation support and participant feedback. Experiences, barriers and support needs will also be examined. In the long term, the project aims to contribute to fairer, clearer and better organised lung cancer screening in Germany.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participation in the 4-IN-THE-LUNG-RUN study at DKFZ or previous assessment within the study; eligibility for lung cancer screening according to current German criteria or additionally according to a risk-based model, particularly PLCOm2012; former or current relevant smoking exposure; willingness to participate in LuCa-GAIN and written informed consent after study information.
Exclusion criteria:
No eligibility for lung cancer screening according to the defined criteria; known lung cancer diagnosis; no written informed consent; medical or technical reasons preventing low-dose CT examination, such as body weight above the CT scanner limit, severe claustrophobia or other relevant contraindications.
